doc.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

chapter: Jaco, Weather Report and pop work
title: Wanting Jaco recognized by the Grammys
summary: Alias says Jaco burned bright and went early, and he pushes the Grammy people to honor him.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: More like some of the Rock ‘n Roll people that you read about who self destruct.

Yeah. He did that. It was almost like he was destined to go out early. You know he came, he was that spark that burned real bright and then disappeared. Now I’m like every time I meet anybody that’s associated with any kind of Grammy thing I always drop that on them. I say when are you guys going to acknowledge Jaco Pastorius? You know we had a monumental concert for him at the Lone Star, you know Paul McCartney showed up and Sting showed up and those guys will tell you about Jaco. I mean why don’t you have like a segment. You know it’s not going to kill you to give him ten minutes or so to say here is a bass player before everybody forgets, here is a bass player that changed the course of music. Give it to him, man, come on.
